Then his wrath will be appeased,

And as the old man said, so it happened.
At that time, a great host of the Nubians set out,
and reached as far as the region of Said (Upper Egypt),
and took many villages captive.
And Saladin heard of it,
and sent an army thither.
And the Arabs encountered the Nubians,
and on both sides many were killed,
while the side of the blacks proved stronger. Then Saladin sent his brother Shams al-Dawlah Turanshah with a large army.
And when they went (he went),
the Nubians fled.
And the Arabs pursued them,
and plundered and killed.
And they seized a fortress called Ibrim,
and placed Arab guards in it.
And when the army of the Arabs returned,
the Nubians returned and retook their fortress.
And the king of the Nubians sent an envoy to Shams al-Dawlah while he was in Qus,
and asked for peace.
Shams al-Dawlah, however, replied
that there would be peace if he paid tribute.
And he sent with the Nubian envoy an envoy of his own, who was called Mas‘ud of Aleppo.
And he went and reached the royal city of the Nubians, which is called Dunqula (Dongola?),
and he saw an impoverished land,
and except for millet, its inhabitants have no grain.
And they have small palm trees,
and with their dates they eat their millet bread,
having nothing else.
And only a single enclosure, which is the palace of the king, exists in it;
and the rest of the people of the city dwell in booths and caves (or huts?):
For that envoy said:
"On one of the days, I saw the king of the Nubians come out naked,
and he mounted a horse likewise naked.
And he had wrapped himself in an unsewn length of satin,
while his head was bare, without hair.
And when I approached and greeted him,
he burst out laughing.
And he commanded, and they branded my hand in the shape of a cross,
and he gave me fifty pounds of flour and dismissed me."
And in the year 569
[569] of the Arabs,
this Shams al-Dawlah, the brother of Saladin, went to the land of Yemen,
and conquered it and reigned over it.
